label: copy-phase input k (k re-fed from original positions 2-4, not the final output)
explanation: Token feature for k, but only during the copy phase. It never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter, and it fires on in_tok k for 99% of its activation mass. Within copy-phase k inputs it is position-gated. It is strongest when the k being fed back came from original position 2-3 (recall_idx 3-4 holds about 80% of mass), weaker at position 4, and near zero when k came from original positions 0-1 (recall_idx <= 2) or on the last copy step (to_go = 0). Bare copy-phase k gives recall 0.98 but precision only 0.26. Adding the position gate brings dev precision to 0.59, recall 0.80, F1 0.68, mass recall 0.89. Many copy-phase k inputs at positions 2-4 still stay silent. The strongest examples tend to have y or q as the next output, but that does not explain most of the mass (y/q-only predicate: mass recall 0.18). Does not fire on other input tokens (k in_tok lift 32x, all other tokens about 0.1x).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=10: k, w, y, h; t=13: k, v, n, y; t=12: k, y, w, v) and the token being output (most: y, q, k, w, 0, 1; least: 3, p, -, o); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=3 & t=5, recall_idx=4.
